messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] hosted-runtime-prod: high OOM rate in kv-cache pool (2165001234)

melissa: noticed a sharp uptick in kv-cache allocations around 2165001200, spike peaked at root ts. 5xx spike ~7% in eu-central.

raj: oncall — looking. any customer impact known?

simon: tracing shows large single-turn prompts leading to unbounded prefetch. continuous-batching is folding extremely long prefixes into batches instead of capping. kv-cache grows without eviction.

aisha: CS: two customers reported mid-stream terminations, one enterprise (Cardinal Labs) on eu cluster. ticket #8122. They saw "stream cut off" and resumed with 500s.

melissa: immediate actions proposed: 1) clamp prefetch per-session to 50k tokens, 2) reduce batching window to 15ms, 3) enable aggressive prefix trimming for sessions > 8k tokens. rolling to a subset first.

raj: apply CLAMP and BATCH changes to eu-pool-a (5 nodes) now. leave prefix-trim as advisory until we can test memory regression.

opsbot: deploybot: rollout started: runtime-config-hotpatch-2165001234 -> eu-pool-a (5 nodes)

6m later

simon: early telemetry: OOM count dropped by ~85% on patched nodes. per-node kv-cache growth dropped from ~90MB/min to ~6MB/min.

melissa: observed overall 5xxs down to ~0.9%. Cardinal Labs confirmed their job completed when retried.

aisha: sent a short customer update: "We deployed a mitigation to throttle very large single-turn prompts while we investigate. Please share any failing request IDs." they replied with logs.

raj: ok. next steps for persistence: - enforce hard per-session cap at runtime (reject new prefetch beyond cap) - add alert: session_kv_cache_bytes > 0.75 * per_gpu_reserve for 2m - change batching heuristic to exclude sessions with extreme prefix length

simon: I already started a PR to add a hard cap + structured 429 response with reason and diagnostic link. will also add a flag to exclude huge prefixes from continuous-batching.

melissa: config we pushed (eu-pool-a):

```
PATCH /admin/runtime/config
{
  "kv_cache.session_prefetch_limit": 50000,
  "batching.max_window_ms": 15,
  "kv_cache.aggressive_prefix_trim_k_tokens": 8
}
```

raj: scheduling a staged rollout to other regions after smoke in eu for 1 hour. julian will take next shift.

julian: taking handoff. will monitor for 3 hours and approve full rollout if stable. added dashboard widget and a temp alert rule. rollback plan ready.

opsbot: deploybot: runtime-hardcap-2165001820 queued for production rollout after manual approval.

melissa: mitigation notes for post-incident: (owner:simon) finish PR and unit tests; (owner:raj) run targeted stress tests in staging with synthetic long single-turn prompts; (owner:aisha) coordinate customer comms and collect failing request IDs; (owner:julian) approve or rollback rollout based on 3-hour window.

simon: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/2387 (adds hard cap + batching exclusion). tests WIP.

melissa: recommendation for immediate telemetry: add sample traces for any session crossing 32k prefetch tokens. quick snapshot helps triage.

raj: agreed. enabled auto-trace sampling for >32k sessions in eu for 2 hours.

aisha: CS update sent. customers asked for ETA on permanent fix; said we'd follow up within 24h with RCA and permanent mitigations.

incident-bot: incident moved out of paging at 2165003899 — mitigations applied, oncall handoff to julian for monitoring.

julian: leaving note: if post-rollout 5xxs exceed 0.5% trigger immediate rollback. will escalate to eng-runtime if metrics worsen.

melissa: closing thread for now. full RCA and kernel traces will be posted in postmortems channel once simon's PR lands and we have reproducible test results.
